title: Futurism & The Aestheticization of Speed
subtitle: The Italian avant-garde movement celebrating machinery and kinetic energy
summary: Founded by F.T. Marinetti in 1909, Futurism embraced technology, dynamic movement, airplanes, and industrial power, rejecting historical academic tradition in favor of kinetic rhythm.
keyTakeaway: Futurism glorified the velocity and violent energy of modern industrial society.

title: Dadaism & Anti-Art Absurdity
subtitle: The radical international movement rejecting bourgeois art conventions
summary: Emerging during WWI, Dada artists like Marcel Duchamp used ready-mades, collage, and nonsensical poetry to protest the rationalist logic that led to mechanical warfare.
keyTakeaway: Dada used absurdity to dismantle conventional definitions of art and institutional power.

title: De Stijl & Neoplasticist Reduction
subtitle: Piet Mondrian and Theo van Doesburg's search for universal harmony
summary: De Stijl reduced art to pure abstraction using only primary colors (red, blue, yellow) alongside black, white, and non-colors constrained within orthogonal horizontal-vertical grids.
keyTakeaway: Neoplasticism sought absolute visual equilibrium through extreme geometric reduction.

title: Constructivism & Art for Social Utility
subtitle: Russian avant-garde movement integrating art directly into industrial life
summary: Constructivists rejected autonomous easel painting, advocating instead that artists become designers, engineers, and typographers producing functional objects for socialist society.
keyTakeaway: Art was stripped of bourgeois decoration to become a direct tool for social transformation.

title: Moral Dumbfounding & Affective Primacy
subtitle: Why humans hold strong moral convictions without rational justification
summary: Studies show people often experience strong gut feelings that an action is morally wrong, yet remain unable to produce any logical rationale when pressed—a state called moral dumbfounding.
keyTakeaway: Moral judgment is driven by immediate emotional gut reactions, with reasoning acting as an post-hoc advocate.

summary: Coined by Leon Festinger, cognitive dissonance occurs when actions contradict beliefs, forcing individuals to rationalize, minimize, or alter their beliefs to restore mental harmony.
keyTakeaway: Human minds prioritize internal consistency over objective truth when resolving internal contradictions.

title: Peak-End Rule & Retrospective Memory Bias
subtitle: How human memory evaluates past experiences based on intensity peaks
summary: Daniel Kahneman demonstrated that human memory does not average an entire event, but evaluates it almost entirely by its peak emotional moment and how it ended.
keyTakeaway: Our retrospective memory is a biased storyteller governed by emotional spikes and final moments.

title: Neuroplasticity & Synaptic Pruning
subtitle: How the brain continuously rewires its neural architecture
summary: Neuroplasticity allows the brain to strengthen active neural pathways while synaptic pruning eliminates unused connections, enabling lifelong learning and recovery from brain injuries.
keyTakeaway: The brain physically restructures its cellular connections in response to continuous habit and thought.

title: Bystander Effect & Diffusion of Responsibility
subtitle: Why individuals fail to offer help when others are present
summary: Social psychological experiments reveal that the presence of multiple onlookers diminishes individual responsibility, as each person assumes someone else will intervene.
keyTakeaway: Group size can paradoxically paralyze individual moral action due to shared responsibility.

subtitle: The automatic physiological synchronization of emotions between humans
summary: Mirror neurons fire both when performing an action and when observing another person perform it, enabling automatic empathetic resonance and micro-facial emotional mirroring.
keyTakeaway: Emotions spread virally through subconscious physiological mirror responses.

subtitle: The tendency to prefer immediate smaller rewards over delayed larger ones
